title: There is no actual-resource inventory: the Studio has never issued an ECS/RDS/CloudFront/S3/SQS/SES/Lambda/ACM call, and /platform renders counts out of a JSON file compiled at a commit
why_open: The ledger says so itself: docs/implementation/system-studio-aws-control-plane-execution-ledger.md:183-185 records, as an honest limit on the FinOps item, that cost by module/cell/environment needs 'the resource tags STUDIO-070-002 defines and a resource graph (STUDIO-080-001), neither of which exists'. The code agrees. apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:3,11 are the only @aws-sdk imports in the whole app, and they are DynamoDB; apps/system-studio/package.json:15-16 declares exactly those two packages and nothing else AWS. The estate the console shows is frozen: apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:7 imports @/generated/platform-truth.json, :341-343 prints 'account {estate.account} · {estate.region}', :346 says 'Read-only inventory of {date}', :351-357 renders estate.summary as chips, :399-404 lists SQS queue names and :406-413 alarm states — every one of them compiled by tools/platform-truth.mjs from docs/architecture/aws-inventory.json, which tools/aws-inventory.mjs produces by shelling out to the aws CLI in a CI workflow (its own header, tools/aws-inventory.mjs:1-24). Not one of the seventeen fields the requirement names exists anywhere in the repository: no ARN, no per-resource state, no stack, no tenant attribution, no dependency edge, no tag map, no security posture, no health, no cost, no drift, no last-change, no retention, no deletion behaviour. The counts in aws-inventory.json are integers with no resource identity behind them, so nothing can be attributed, diffed or drilled into.
smallest_real_change: One adapter, apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/inventory.ts, that per service issues the paginated List/Describe through the shared lib/aws/client.ts and maps each item onto ONE shape: EstateResource { arn, resourceType, name, state, region, accountId, partition, tags, attribution: {tenantSlug} | {shared: true} | {unattributed: true}, dependsOn: string[], asOf }. Attribution comes from the `tenure:tenant` tag resolved through resourcegroupstaggingapi:GetResources in lib/aws/tags.ts — never from a name heuristic, because a heuristic that guesses wrong attributes one tenant's bill to another. Dependency edges come only from ids the describe responses already carry (service→cluster ARN, service→targetGroupArn, distribution→origin domain name, DB instance→DBSubnetGroup/VpcSecurityGroups), so no edge is invented. Give each surface its own named refresh constant in the module (ECS_SERVICES_REFRESH_MS, RDS_REFRESH_MS, ACM_REFRESH_MS, S3_REFRESH_MS …) rather than one global, hold a short server-side cache keyed on surface+region, and back off on ThrottlingException. Every call returns the Probe/Result union so a denial renders 'unknown' with the principal and the minimum IAM statement — this shares lib/aws/result.ts with the item surveyor 1 filed as STUDIO-000-007 and surveyor 6 as STUDIO-140-007, and must be built once. Add the route at apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/estate/page.tsx, add it to Nav ENTRIES (apps/system-studio/src/components/Nav.tsx:19-22) AND to the layout spec's ROUTES array (apps/system-studio/e2e/layout.spec.ts:40), or the contrast and table-overflow assertions never see the new page. Register lib/aws/client.ts in OWNERS.aws at tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs:198-207 and add it to the `proof` list at :397-402, otherwise 'no module outside its adapter imports an AWS client' reds on the first import. Add the new @aws-sdk/client-* packages to apps/system-studio/package.json and run `npm install --package-lock-only` (tests/architecture/lockfile-knows-every-workspace.test.mjs catches the omission locally). Proof: for EACH service adapter, a test whose stand-in `send` returns AccessDeniedException, ThrottlingException, an empty-but-successful page, and a populated page, asserting FOUR different rendered outputs; then mutate inventory.ts (not the helper) to swallow AccessDenied into [] and confirm the empty-vs-unknown case reds.

title: The account topology is neither declared nor read: the only account id in the Studio is a hardcoded literal, and region/partition fall back to us-east-1/aws on a residency-critical path
why_open: Nothing in apps/system-studio ever asks AWS which accounts exist. `estate.organizationInUse`, rendered at apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:361-363, comes from the frozen generated JSON, whose value was set by a CI-time `aws organizations describe-organization` that was DENIED — tools/aws-inventory.mjs:66-68 issues it and :55 records the denial. The one place the Studio names an account is a literal: apps/system-studio/src/lib/cells.ts:62 `awsAccountId: env("AWS_ACCOUNT_ID", "047385673922")`, with region defaulting at :55 to "us-east-1" and partition at :65 to "aws" — and cells.ts is on the EXEMPT list at tests/security/no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:36, so the guard written specifically to stop compiled-in estate facts does not cover the one file that has them. That is not cosmetic: apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:64,68 feeds `fleet()[0]?.region` and `fleet()[0]?.partition` into `availabilityDecisions`, whose own comment at :57-62 says a capability may be offered only when the decision passes for the exact region — so an unset AWS_REGION silently offers capabilities as if the estate were in us-east-1 in the `aws` partition. That is the GE-010-007 data-residency defect class exactly. And the twelve account roles the requirement names (Organizations management, Control Tower/log archive, security/audit, identity/shared services, network/edge, control-plane prod, control-plane nonprod, tooling/build, regional cells, dedicated tenants, backup/DR, sandbox) are declared nowhere in the repository — grep finds no list of them in packages/, infrastructure/ or docs/architecture/, so there is nothing to reconcile a live read against.
smallest_real_change: Declare the topology as data — apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/topology.ts exporting ACCOUNT_ROLES: { key, purpose, requiredWhen: (scale) => boolean } for the twelve roles — then reconcile it against a live organizations:DescribeOrganization + ListAccounts + ListTagsForResource read in lib/aws/organization.ts, rendering three columns: role, the account actually filling it, and the verdict. When Organizations is not in use the verdict is 'single-account estate, this role is filled by <account from STS>'; when the call is DENIED the verdict is UNKNOWN with the principal ARN and `organizations:ListAccounts` — never 'not in use', because those are opposite facts. Then make cells.ts:62 read the account id, region and partition from the STS-resolved identity (lib/aws/identity.ts, GetCallerIdentity, partition parsed off the returned Arn) with the env vars as an explicit override rather than the other way round, and DELETE the cells.ts entry from tests/security/no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:36 EXEMPT — that deletion is the proof the literal is gone, and the guard then fails if anyone re-adds one. Check every consumer of fleet() before changing what it returns: apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:64,68, apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:65, apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/page.tsx:42, apps/system-studio/src/lib/adopt.ts:84,194,242, apps/system-studio/src/lib/cells.ts:112,124. `fleet()` throws FleetMisconfigured today (cells.ts:90) so making the identity read a hard dependency turns a page into a 500 — resolve identity lazily and let a cell whose account is UNKNOWN report that rather than throw. Proof: a test that runs `availabilityDecisions` twice with a stand-in identity in eu-west-1 vs us-east-1 and asserts a residency-restricted capability is refused in one and offered in the other; mutate cells.ts back to the literal fallback and confirm it reds.

title: Orphan detection does not exist — the only orphan finding in the product is a paragraph a human wrote into the inventory JSON, which is precisely the computation this item asks for
why_open: No module compares IaC, tags, the registry, Config, service APIs, CUR and a relationship graph, because five of those seven inputs have no reader at all. The Studio's only estate-shaped registry read is `listTenants` (apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:181-216) whose ProjectionExpression is slug/state/displayName/updatedAt/isolation — it returns nothing about resources. There is no live service-API read (registry.ts:3 is the only AWS import). There is no tag read (no resourcegroupstaggingapi anywhere). There is no CUR: apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts:83-89 `readCurLines` throws by construction, so 'expected cost' has no source. What the product DOES show is the giveaway: apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:392-404 renders a hand-written section titled 'Queues with no producer and no consumer' — a real orphan finding, discovered by a person, typed into docs/architecture/aws-inventory.json, and frozen. That is one orphan, found once, by hand. The requirement asks the engine to find them continuously and attach an owner and an expected cost to each, and neither the owner field nor the cost field exists on any resource shape in the repository.
smallest_real_change: apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/orphans.ts taking four inputs — the live resources from lib/aws/inventory.ts, the tagged set from lib/aws/tags.ts, the tenant slugs from registry.listTenants(), and the Terraform-managed ARNs (parsed from infrastructure/studio/outputs.tf + infrastructure/terraform/outputs.tf, or a committed manifest of managed ARNs) — and returning Orphan { arn, why: 'no-tenure-tag' | 'tenant-not-in-registry' | 'not-in-iac' | 'tagged-owner-unknown', owner: string | 'UNOWNED', expectedMonthlyCost: Money | null }. Two rules decide whether this is honest. First, expectedMonthlyCost is `null`, never zero, when Cost Explorer is unreachable or the resource carries no billed line — zero reads as free and is the exact number that gets an orphan ignored. Second, if ANY of the four inputs arrived in the `unknown` (denied/throttled) arm, the verdict for the affected scope is `unknown` with the missing input named, not 'no orphans found': an operator told a bucket has no orphans when the tag API was denied is being told the opposite of the truth. Delete the hand-written 'Queues with no producer and no consumer' section at apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:392-404 in the same change and let the computed list render there — leaving both would give the console two answers. Proof: a test with a populated inventory and a registry listing that omits one tagged tenant, asserting the resource is reported 'tenant-not-in-registry' and NOT silently attributed; then a second run where the tag call returns AccessDenied, asserting the verdict is unknown; mutate orphans.ts to treat a denied tag read as 'no tag' and confirm the second case reds.

title: The Studio's AWS role holds no read permission at all and no explicit Deny on destructive verbs, so 'understand every resource without unsafe mutation access' has neither half
why_open: infrastructure/studio/iam.tf:36-43 creates the running task's role with the comment 'Deliberately empty: the Studio reads configuration that ships in its image and talks to nothing else. An engine that needs no AWS permissions should hold none.' The only policy attached to it anywhere is infrastructure/studio/dynamodb.tf:68-96, and its Allow statement (:77-83) grants GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, Query, Scan and TransactWriteItems on the registry table — i.e. the Studio's sole AWS authority today is WRITE authority over the registry, with zero read authority over the estate. So an operator can understand nothing about a tenant's AWS resources, which is the first half of the gate failing outright. The second half has no guard: the Deny statement at dynamodb.tf:89-95 covers only dynamodb:DeleteItem and dynamodb:DeleteTable, and there is no test anywhere asserting the Studio's role cannot mutate an AWS resource — tests/security/ has operator-boundary, operator-plane-content and oidc-trust, none of which parse infrastructure/studio/*.tf. The moment a read plane is added the cheapest thing to write is a broad `Allow` on Describe*/List*/ecs:* and nothing would catch it.
smallest_real_change: A SEPARATE `aws_iam_role_policy` in infrastructure/studio/iam.tf named `estate-read`, listing only the exact Describe/List/Get actions the read adapters call (one line per action, no wildcards), plus an explicit `Effect = "Deny"` statement over the destructive verbs — ecs:DeleteService, ecs:UpdateService, ecs:StopTask, rds:DeleteDBInstance, rds:ModifyDBInstance, s3:DeleteBucket, s3:DeleteObject, cloudfront:DeleteDistribution, acm:DeleteCertificate, kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion, iam:*, organizations:LeaveOrganization — written as Deny because an Allow added later cannot override it. Then the guard that makes it stick: tests/security/studio-role-cannot-mutate.test.mjs, which reads infrastructure/studio/*.tf, extracts every action inside an Allow attached to aws_iam_role.task, and asserts each matches /^(sts:GetCallerIdentity|ce:Get|organizations:(Describe|List)|tag:Get|[a-z0-9-]+:(Describe|List|Get|BatchGet))/ with the six DynamoDB write actions named as explicit, reasoned exceptions; and asserts the Deny statement exists with at least the verbs above. Prove it by adding `ecs:UpdateService` to the Allow and confirming the test reds, then removing it. The other half of the gate — 'and dependency' — is the dependsOn edges from STUDIO-080-001; this item is not true until the estate page renders a resource's dependents, so build them together. Update docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md's 'Deployment identity' section in the same change so the documented posture matches the applied one.

title: Residual retention is INFERRED from four registry booleans, never observed from AWS, and the 'residual charge' is a prose sentence with no number behind it
why_open: packages/provisioning/src/residual-reconciliation.ts:148-157 defines ObservedTenantResources as exactly { isolation, hasDeployment, serving, evidenceRecords }, and its single production caller — apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/page.tsx:131-136 — fills all four from the registry record (`tenant.manifest.isolation`, `tenant.deployment !== undefined`, `tenant.deployment?.serving === true`, `tenant.evidence.length`). So `observeResidual` (residual-reconciliation.ts:173) concludes 'this tenant retains rows, objects and backups' from whether a deployment manifest was ever PUBLISHED — not from an RDS snapshot, an S3 object version, a log group's retentionInDays, a Backup recovery point, a KMS key or a Route 53 record set, which are six of the ten things the requirement names. Nothing in the repository reads any of them. The charge half is worse: RESIDUAL_COST (packages/provisioning/src/lifecycle.ts:130-134) is a Record<TenantState, string> built out of claim NOTES, rendered as a sentence at apps/system-studio/src/lib/fleet-health.ts:145 (`residualCost: RESIDUAL_COST[input.state] ?? null`) and pasted into the risk panel at apps/system-studio/src/lib/tenant-state.ts:124. There is no money anywhere on the path, and the only cost reader in the app throws (apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts:83-89). So a HIBERNATED_ZERO_RUNTIME tenant and one still running a dedicated task render the same residual sentence and the same absent charge — which is precisely the failure the requirement's last line calls out.
smallest_real_change: Add a SECOND, separately-typed observation rather than widening the first. apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/retained.ts reads, filtered by the `tenure:tenant` tag: rds:DescribeDBSnapshots, s3:ListObjectVersions on the tenant prefix (bytes and version count), logs:DescribeLogGroups (retentionInDays and storedBytes), backup:ListRecoveryPoints, kms:ListKeys/ListResourceTags, route53:ListResourceRecordSets — returning RetainedResources { snapshots, objectVersions, logBytes, recoveryPoints, keys, recordSets, legalHolds, asOf } where every field is the Probe union so a denial is UNKNOWN, not zero. Then make `residualFindings` (apps/system-studio/src/lib/tenant-state.ts:88) take that as a REQUIRED third parameter — do NOT add optional fields to ObservedTenantResources: its one construction site is tenants/[slug]/page.tsx:131 and an optional field that caller does not set is invisible to tsc and would silently keep reporting 'nothing unexplained', which is the answer an operator most wants to be true. A required parameter makes tsc name the caller. For the charge, add lib/aws/cost-explorer.ts calling ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources with a tag filter on `tenure:tenant` and GroupBy SERVICE, mapping each result straight onto the existing CostLine shape (packages/finops/src/allocation.ts:47-77) so buildCostReport and the whole allocation engine need no change — and keep the CUR arm of cost-source.ts intact, since only a CUR reconciles to the invoice. Render '$0.00 retained' only when Cost Explorer actually answered; render UNKNOWN when it did not. Proof: two runs of the tenant page for a HIBERNATED_ZERO_RUNTIME tenant, one where DescribeDBSnapshots returns a snapshot and one where it returns an empty page, asserting the residual panel says something different; then a third where it returns AccessDenied, asserting UNKNOWN. Mutate tenants/[slug]/page.tsx to pass an empty RetainedResources and confirm the first case reds.

title: The high-risk confirmation is a display, not a gate — it takes no input, the server action never receives a typed target, and no test asserts a refusal for a missing step-up or an unbound approval
why_open: apps/system-studio/src/components/states.tsx:265-280 `HighRiskConfirmation` renders target/impact/policy/approval/reversibility as a <dl> and accepts no value from the operator; apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/AdvanceControls.tsx:64 places it beside the submit control. The server action enforces exactly two things: lifecycle legality, and that the approver is a different, allowlisted operator — apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:635 `approverIsOperator: approvedBy ? isOperator(approvedBy) : undefined`. There is no typed target confirmation (nothing reads a field the operator must type), no step-up (auth.ts:21-55 is a single credentials provider with a JWT session and no re-authentication anywhere), no semantic permission (apps/system-studio/src/lib/operators.ts:110 `isOperator` is one flat allowlist — every operator can do everything), and no digest binding between the risk an approver READ and the transition that executes (`digestOf` is applied to the manifest at registry.ts:270 and 352, never to the risk summary). For the AWS mutation surface this cluster is meant to add, none of it exists at all. And there is no test asserting any of these refusals: apps/system-studio/e2e/states-logic.spec.ts asserts the component renders its five fields, which is a rendering assertion, not a fail-closed one.
smallest_real_change: Make the confirmation an INPUT. Give `HighRiskConfirmation` a required `confirm: { label, expected }` prop that renders a text field the operator must fill, and a hidden `riskDigest` field holding a hash of the five rendered facts. In the server action, recompute the risk from the same inputs, hash it, and REFUSE unless (a) the submitted digest equals the recomputed one — an approver who read a different consequence did not approve this one, (b) the typed value equals the target slug (or ARN, for an AWS mutation), and (c) the existing approver checks still pass. Add a REFUSED_IRREVERSIBLE arm to lib/aws/mutate.ts for terminate/delete/revoke/scale-to-zero-on-a-serving-resource that returns the AWS CLI command a human can run themselves and NEVER calls the SDK — `canReachServing` (tenant-state.ts:43) already computes irreversibility for lifecycle moves and is the model. Every mutation writes its audit row through the Studio audit ledger BEFORE it acts and its outcome after (shares lib/audit-ledger.ts with STUDIO-110-005 and surveyor 6's STUDIO-060-010 — one file, one agent). Proof, five separate cases, each mutating the ACTION and not the helper: wrong digest; missing typed target; actor === approver; approver not on the allowlist; destructive verb. Each must produce a DIFFERENT refusal message, so a test asserting 'it refused' cannot pass for the wrong reason. Add apps/system-studio/e2e/high-risk-fails-closed.spec.ts driving the real form.

title: The Studio writes no audit row at all, and the audit package's read half — verifyChain, applyRetention, legal holds — has no production caller anywhere in the repository
why_open: A case-insensitive grep for 'audit' across apps/system-studio/src returns exactly two hits, both doc comments about future intent: apps/system-studio/src/lib/config-store.ts:25 and apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:133. There is no @tenure/audit dependency in apps/system-studio/package.json:14-23. And the ratchet that would notice does not look here: tests/security/audit-writes.test.mjs:31 sets SOURCE_GLOBS to ['apps/web/src/**/*.ts', 'apps/web/src/**/*.tsx'] only, so every Studio action — composing a tenant, adopting one, advancing a lifecycle state, publishing a configuration revision, and every denial — is outside audit coverage entirely. The registry's STEP rows (registry.ts:500-511) are a lifecycle history: they carry from/to/at/actor/reason/attempt and have no outcome, no ALLOW/DENY, no redaction and no hash. Separately, the verification half of the requirement exists as code with no caller: `verifyChain` (packages/audit/src/verify.ts:96) and `applyRetention` (packages/audit/src/retention.ts) are referenced only from packages/audit/src/audit.test.ts — nothing in apps/ calls either, so 'verification tooling' and 'retention' are declarations. Finally 'centralized protected storage' is not true of the one table involved: infrastructure/studio/dynamodb.tf:77-83 grants the Studio's own role PutItem AND UpdateItem on the registry table, and the Deny at :89-95 covers only DeleteItem/DeleteTable — so an audit row written there could be rewritten in place by the very process that wrote it.
smallest_real_change: Note this shares apps/system-studio/src/lib/audit-ledger.ts with surveyor 6's STUDIO-060-010 (the change record); build the writer once and take the three halves this item adds. (1) Storage that cannot be rewritten: write chained rows as pk=AUDIT#<tenant|PLATFORM>, sk=SEQ#<zero-padded sequence> through a new `putAuditRow` in registry.ts using ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(sk) — registry.ts is the only module allowed to hold a DynamoDB client (tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs:204) so the write belongs there — and REMOVE dynamodb:UpdateItem from the Allow at infrastructure/studio/dynamodb.tf:80, adding it to the Deny at :89-95 instead, since nothing in registry.ts issues an UpdateCommand today (it uses Put/Get/Query/Scan/TransactWrite only) so removing it costs nothing and closes the rewrite path. (2) Verification tooling with a real caller: a /platform/audit page calling verifyChain over the rows read back through registry.queryTenantItems, rendering breaks, gaps and duplicates by sequence — add the route to Nav.tsx ENTRIES and to e2e/layout.spec.ts:40 ROUTES. (3) Retention: call applyRetention with an explicit legal-hold list and render the deletion PLAN without performing it, which is what that function already returns. (4) Extend tests/security/audit-writes.test.mjs's SOURCE_GLOBS to include apps/system-studio/src so the Studio is inside the ratchet, with the raw-write ceiling left at 32 — the Studio must add zero raw writes. Proof: seed three chained rows, tamper with the middle row's content, assert verifyChain reports the break at that sequence and the page renders it; then mutate the WRITER (audit-ledger.ts) to omit previousHash and confirm the page reds rather than showing an intact chain.

title: Execution records carry step, attempt and result and nothing else — no input/output digest pair, no assumed-role session, no resource handle, no AWS request id, no next-retry, no compensation
why_open: The whole persisted execution shape is packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:56-65: StepEvidence { step, state, ok, digest?, detail, checks? }. It is built in one place (execute.ts:152) and written by apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:500-511 alongside LifecycleStep { from, to, at, actor, reason, attempt } (registry.ts:245-251 reads them back). Of the twelve fields the requirement names, three are present: step, attempt, result. `digest?` is a single optional output digest — there is no input digest, so nothing can tell 'this step ran on the configuration the approver saw' from 'this step ran on whatever was current'. There is no assumed-role session (no sts:AssumeRole call exists anywhere in the repository), no resource handle (no ARN is ever stored — see STUDIO-080-001), no AWS request id (`requestId` and `$metadata` appear nowhere in apps/system-studio/src or packages/), no next-retry time and no scheduler that would honour one, and no compensation record — `attempt` is derived from history in `advance` rather than from any retry policy. So the item's own words, 'safe failure, next retry, compensation, and evidence', are three-quarters unrepresented.
smallest_real_change: Add a REQUIRED `execution` block to StepEvidence rather than optional fields: execution: { inputDigest, outputDigest, awsRequestIds: readonly string[], assumedRoleArn: string | null, resourceHandles: readonly string[], nextRetryAt: string | null, compensation: { of: string; ok: boolean; detail: string } | null }. Required, because an optional block that a caller forgets compiles clean, passes every unit test that builds its own fixture, and shows an operator a step with no provenance. Before changing the type, fix every construction and consumption site in the same change — the builder at packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:152, the write at apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:500-511, the read-back at registry.ts:249-251, the deploymentManifest input at execute.ts:498, the caller in apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts, and the evidence panel on apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/page.tsx. Feed awsRequestIds by having lib/aws/client.ts return { value, requestId } from every send (the SDK already exposes it on `$metadata.requestId`) and threading them up — that is what makes the field real rather than an empty array everyone passes. inputDigest hashes the resolved configuration + module set the step ran against, using the same `digestOf` registry.ts:270 already uses, so the two cannot disagree. Proof: mutate apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts (the PRODUCER) to pass an empty awsRequestIds and assert the tenant page's evidence panel reds — a test that calls the builder directly would stay green when the action stops using it, which is exactly the failure mode this programme has already paid for.

title: The only diff in the product is a human-readable string over app configuration; nine of the ten domains the requirement names — including AWS resources and cost — have no diff at all, and no diff has a machine-readable form
why_open: apps/system-studio/src/lib/revisions.ts:64 `compareRevisions(before, after)` returns ValueDifference[] over resolved configuration values, and :82 `renderComparison` collapses it to a STRING. Nothing emits a machine-readable diff document: there is no JSON representation, no route serving one, and no contract for one — packages/contracts/src/index.ts publishes fifteen parsers (parseTenantContext:162, parseCommand:228, parseQuery:280, parseDomainEvent:361, parseOutboxRecord:424, parseContractError:489, parseJobRequest:535, parseIdempotencyRecord:582, parsePermissionCheck:664, parsePermissionDecision:682, parseFileRef:716, parseConfigSnapshot:770, parseAuditEntry:816, parseToolRegistration:861, parseProcessChain:938) and none is a diff, plan or change. Of the ten domains listed — app config, data/schema, IAM/security, AWS resources, domains, integrations, Relay, cost, operations, rollback — exactly one is implemented. The AWS-resources arm cannot exist yet because actual AWS state is never read (apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:3 is the only AWS import in the app), and the cost arm cannot because the cost reader throws (apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts:83-89). `previewPlanCost` exists in packages/finops/src/reporting.ts but the ledger records at docs/implementation/system-studio-aws-control-plane-execution-ledger.md:211-215 that it is 'published and computable but not yet enforced at execution time' with no pipeline to wire into.
smallest_real_change: Define the machine-readable form FIRST and derive the human one from it, so the two cannot disagree. Add `ChangeDiff` + `parseChangeDiff` to packages/contracts/src/index.ts in the same refusal style as the other fifteen: { schemaVersion, entries: Array<{ domain: 'app-config'|'data-schema'|'iam'|'aws-resource'|'domain'|'integration'|'relay'|'cost'|'operations'|'rollback', path, before, after, effect: 'create'|'update'|'delete'|'replace', reversible: boolean, monthlyCostDeltaMinor: number|null }> }. Rewrite apps/system-studio/src/lib/revisions.ts:82 `renderComparison` to take that document rather than ValueDifference[] — it is a pure function with one production caller in the configuration editor plus the publication plan, so the change is contained. Add the aws-resource arm as apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/drift.ts, diffing the live inventory from STUDIO-080-001 against the desired set and emitting entries with `effect` and `reversible` set from what the resource actually is (a delete of an RDS instance is not reversible; a desired-count change is). Attach the cost arm by populating monthlyCostDeltaMinor from `previewPlanCost` (packages/finops/src/reporting.ts) so the existing threshold policy at apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/cost/page.tsx:100-130 finally has a number to assess. Leave the seven unimplemented domains OUT of the enum rather than emitting empty arrays for them — an empty 'integrations' section reads as 'nothing changed', which is not what 'we do not compute this' means. title: No versioned control-plane contract exists for resources, cost or drift — the contracts package has fifteen shapes, none of them control-plane, and carries no version field at all
why_open: packages/contracts/src/index.ts is the repository's contract surface and its fifteen exported parsers (enumerated at lines 162, 228, 280, 361, 424, 489, 535, 582, 664, 682, 716, 770, 816, 861, 938) cover tenant context, commands, queries, domain events, outbox records, errors, jobs, idempotency, permissions, files, config snapshots, audit entries, tool registrations and process chains. Not one of the eleven the requirement names — tenants, manifests, plans, approvals, executions, resources, releases, lifecycle, evidence, cost, drift — is there. There is no OpenAPI document and no AsyncAPI document anywhere in the repository. And 'versioned' is not merely unpublished but unrepresented: the package exports no CONTRACT_VERSION or schemaVersion field on any shape, so there is no mechanism by which a consumer could refuse an incompatible producer. The shapes that WOULD need contracts exist only as TypeScript interfaces inside app code, which the package's own header (index.ts:1-22) explains is exactly the thing that constrains nothing at a module boundary — TenantRecord at apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:90-112 and CostReport at apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-report.ts:26-41 are both erased at build time and both cross a process boundary the moment anything reads them over HTTP.
smallest_real_change: Add the three the live read plane will actually emit, because those are the ones no other package owns and the only ones that can get a production caller today: `parseEstateResource`, `parseCostFigure` and `parseDriftFinding` in packages/contracts/src/index.ts, each carrying an explicit `schemaVersion` and each refusing an unknown MAJOR (a minor it does not recognise is forward-compatible; a major is not). Give them a production caller in the same change — apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/inventory.ts parses its own mapped output through parseEstateResource before returning it, so a service adapter that starts emitting a malformed resource is refused at the boundary rather than rendered. Generate the JSON Schema FROM those parsers into docs/contracts/*.schema.json at build time and add tests/architecture/contracts-schemas-match-parsers.test.mjs asserting the committed schema admits exactly what the parser admits over a table of accept/reject fixtures — a schema hand-written beside a parser is the artefact that drifts, and a schema generated from a second source is the same problem with more steps. This neighbours surveyor 6's STUDIO-130-002 (the API envelope and problem-details work in apps/system-studio/src/lib/api/); the envelope should carry the contract's schemaVersion, so land them together. Proof: mutate parseEstateResource to accept a missing `arn` and confirm both the schema-match test and the inventory adapter's rejection case red.
